steps.title: Establish the shared app architecture and platform foundations
steps.summary: From November 2026 to February 2027, establish the product, architecture and technical foundations for the Student Experience Hub. Define the route from the Edge-led build into a wider student app and put in place the shared environments, hosting, release infrastructure, identity, interface, integration, observability, assurance and service patterns needed to build and operate student-facing capabilities coherently.

outputs.title: Product and transition blueprint
outputs.summary: Define the Hub product boundary, target journeys, transition from King’s Edge and relationship to authoritative source systems.

outputs.title: Azure environments and hosting model
outputs.summary: Establish the agreed development, test and production environment pattern, hosting responsibilities and cost model.

outputs.title: Delivery and release infrastructure
outputs.summary: Establish source-control, build, deployment, release, testing and rollback arrangements for the shared app.

outputs.title: Identity, permissions and profile foundations
outputs.summary: Define reusable authentication, authorisation, role and student-profile patterns.

outputs.title: Shared application shell and design system
outputs.summary: Define the common navigation, interface components, responsive behaviour and accessible design standards.

outputs.title: Data, API and integration conventions
outputs.summary: Agree how the Hub uses authoritative data and reusable interfaces in coordination with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems.

outputs.title: Telemetry, monitoring and recovery
outputs.summary: Establish analytics, logging, performance monitoring, alerting, resilience and recovery patterns.

outputs.title: Privacy, security and accessibility controls
outputs.summary: Embed the technical controls and assurance requirements needed for supported student-facing operation.

outputs.title: Platform documentation and ownership
outputs.summary: Document the foundations and identify the product, platform and service responsibilities needed to sustain them.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide architecture authority, Azure and DevOps expertise, identity design and platform engineering for the shared app foundations.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: The Hub may be built without an agreed, supportable platform and identity model.

existingCapacity.owner: Digital and IT with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems
existingCapacity.contribution: Provide authoritative-data, API and integration expertise so the Hub does not create a separate or duplicated data layer.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Student journeys may rely on incomplete, duplicated or weakly governed data and integrations.

existingCapacity.contribution: Provide scheduled security, privacy, accessibility, performance, monitoring, recovery and live-service expertise.
existingCapacity.riskIfMissing: Capabilities may not be secure, accessible, reliable or supportable in production.

newInvestment.item: Year 1 Student Experience Hub platform and delivery costs
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers Azure and related platform consumption, standard environments and tooling, and targeted migration, integration, assurance and testing support. It assumes maximum use of existing institutional licences, specialists and standard provision. Staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The shared app foundations and first live capabilities may not have the environments, platform services or targeted specialist support needed for safe operation.

enablingConditions.condition: Approve the initial app architecture, hosting and platform route in time to support the King’s Edge replatform.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the Student Experience Hub sponsor
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Edge-led build may create technical choices that are difficult to reuse or support.

enablingConditions.condition: Assign named architecture, platform, identity, data, integration and assurance contributors with protected availability and decision rights.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The app foundations may be delayed by competing specialist queues.

enablingConditions.condition: Operate one coordinated product pipeline across 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4, with app and platform investment held under 4.1.2 and shared staffing held under 4.1.3.
enablingConditions.owner: King’s Edge Portfolio Board and Digital and IT
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: Investment and capacity may be fragmented or double-counted.

enablingConditions.condition: Validate the platform cost envelopes through a costed solution design and confirmed institutional licence and hosting arrangements.
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The budget may not reflect the actual platform and operating model.

steps.title: Build the reusable Hub kernel through King’s Edge
steps.summary: From March to June 2027, turn the shared foundations into a reusable Hub kernel, using the replatformed King’s Edge service as the first substantial live product. Establish reusable application-shell, navigation, profile, permissions, interface, telemetry and integration capabilities without making King’s Edge a separate long-term platform.

outputs.title: Reusable application kernel
outputs.summary: Create the common shell, navigation, session and interface capabilities that can support more than one student journey.

outputs.title: Shared identity and profile use
outputs.summary: Apply the agreed identity, role, permission and student-profile patterns in a live product.

outputs.title: Reusable analytics and telemetry
outputs.summary: Implement consistent product analytics, service monitoring and journey measurement.

outputs.title: Authoritative-data integration
outputs.summary: Use reusable interfaces and appropriate authoritative data rather than building a separate Edge-owned data layer.

outputs.title: Production service patterns
outputs.summary: Apply the agreed deployment, assurance, monitoring, support and recovery arrangements in live delivery.

outputs.title: Documented reusable components
outputs.summary: Identify and document which parts of the Edge-led implementation form the initial Hub component set.

steps.title: Prove and harden the Hub kernel through live Edge use
steps.summary: Use the 2027 King’s Edge product releases and controlled pilots to test the shared app and platform patterns under real use. Resolve weaknesses, harden reusable components, establish performance and cost evidence, and document what is ready to support the first wider student journeys.

outputs.title: Live pattern validation
outputs.summary: Test identity, navigation, interface, data, integration, analytics, accessibility and operational patterns through real student and staff use.

outputs.title: Hardened shared components
outputs.summary: Resolve weaknesses and prepare the components that are genuinely reusable beyond King’s Edge.

outputs.title: Reusable pattern library
outputs.summary: Document approved components, interfaces, conventions and constraints for wider app delivery.

outputs.title: Platform performance and cost baseline
outputs.summary: Establish evidence on reliability, performance, consumption and support requirements.

outputs.title: Wider-app readiness evidence
outputs.summary: Identify the technical and product gaps that must be addressed before the first non-Edge journeys are released.

newInvestment.item: Year 2 Student Experience Hub platform and delivery costs
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers live platform consumption and targeted integration, migration, technical assurance and production testing costs that cannot be absorbed through existing institutional capacity. Staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: Live operating costs or essential platform work may displace the planned Hub product roadmap.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the Year 2 app and platform profile against the confirmed roadmap and actual platform consumption.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub product and platform leadership with Finance
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The platform budget may not match the confirmed live-service footprint.

steps.title: Approve the wider app roadmap and first non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: From March to April 2028, consolidate the Edge-focused Hub kernel, confirm which capabilities are ready for wider reuse, select the first priority student journeys beyond King’s Edge, and agree the migration, integration and product sequence for the next phase. Align the roadmap explicitly with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems and the readiness of 4.1.1 Student Relationship and CRM Foundation.

steps.title: Launch the shared student app with the first non-Edge journeys
steps.summary: Turn the Edge-led environment into a common student app by introducing a shared home, navigation and profile, connecting authoritative data made available through 1.2, and releasing the first selected journeys beyond King’s Edge. Maintain authoritative source systems where appropriate while allowing students to complete useful parts of a journey within the common product.

newInvestment.item: Year 3 Student Experience Hub platform and delivery costs
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before the 2028/29 app and platform plan is fixed
newInvestment.fundingRoute: TBC through the mobilisation business case
newInvestment.rationale: Covers the larger live platform footprint and targeted integration, migration, assurance and transition costs that cannot be absorbed internally. Staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The wider app integration and transition may not be completed or operated safely.

enablingConditions.condition: Reset the final mobilisation-year app and platform profile against actual consumption, the confirmed wider-app roadmap and the remaining integration and migration work.
enablingConditions.owner: Student Experience Hub product and platform leadership
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The budget may not match the scale and support obligations of the expanding shared app.

steps.title: Expand integrated journeys and common app capabilities
steps.summary: Add further priority journeys and mature the capabilities shared across them, including common search, actions, communications, notifications, personalisation, self-service and system integration. Bring King’s Edge fully into the shared product environment and begin reducing duplicated entry points where the app can replace them safely and usefully.

steps.title: Make wider student journeys the primary product roadmap
steps.summary: Shift the centre of product demand from King’s Edge to the broader student experience. Integrate additional systems and service journeys, introduce CRM-enabled interactions as 4.1.1 becomes ready, and use common Hub capabilities to help students navigate information, opportunities, actions, progress and support through a more coherent institutional relationship.

steps.title: Consolidate the Hub and rationalise parallel entry points
steps.summary: Establish the Student Experience Hub as the primary student-facing product and platform, with enduring product ownership, platform governance, service management, cost ownership and product analytics. Progressively retire or rationalise duplicated portals and repeated functionality where continuity is assured, while retaining specialist source systems and interfaces where they continue to add necessary value.

newInvestment.item: Business-as-usual Student Experience Hub platform operating costs
newInvestment.category: recurrent digital app and platform costs
newInvestment.estimatedCost: Indicative £60,000 annual recurrent envelope in constant 2026 prices.
newInvestment.decisionNeededBy: Before recurrent budgets are fixed for 2029/30
newInvestment.fundingRoute: Recurrent Digital and IT baseline, TBC
newInvestment.rationale: Covers production platform operation and the limited tooling, specialist technical assurance and contingency that cannot be absorbed through existing Digital and IT services. Recurrent staffing is held separately under 4.1.3.
newInvestment.riskIfMissing: The Hub may lack the operating budget required to remain secure, reliable and supportable.

enablingConditions.condition: Confirm enduring product, platform and service ownership and replace the recurrent envelope with an agreed service-cost model based on actual consumption and support obligations.
enablingConditions.owner: Digital and IT with the accountable Student Experience Hub sponsor and Finance
enablingConditions.decisionNeededBy: Before transition to business as usual
enablingConditions.riskIfMissing: The Hub may enter business as usual without clear accountability or a credible operating budget.
